text: To thwart someone is to stop their plan from working. In the movie, the heroine goes back in time to block the evil computer's plans.
Something jarring clashes with what came before, so it feels harsh or startling. The film's pictures changed style from scene to scene, and viewers disliked that clash.
Credible means believable. The computer-made actors' faces did not look like real feelings, so viewers did not believe them.
Short for science fiction: made-up stories about science and technology, like time travel and robots.
Cinemas are the movie theaters where people pay to watch films on a big screen.
Here, features is a verb. It means the film has a certain person or thing as an important part. It is not the plural noun for a face's parts.
To go to a moment in the past. It is a favorite idea in science-fiction stories.
Here, plots are secret plans, usually to do something bad. Plots can also mean the events of a story, but not in this sentence.
An invented word for a computer far smarter than any person. The movie's villain is one.
Ironic means the opposite of what you would expect. It is odd that the film about an evil AI was made using AI.
Tools and machines made with science. Here it means AI software that can make videos.
To threaten something is to be a danger to it. In the movie, the evil AI is a danger to all people.
When something is wrecked so badly it is gone. The story says AI might destroy humankind.
All human beings. Many writers now say humankind.
The opening part of a movie where the title and credits appear. Here, the film states that AI made it.
Made or produced. AI-generated video means a computer program created the pictures, not a camera filming real things.
Computer programs that can do things that normally need human thinking, like making pictures or writing. People shorten it to AI.
A computer program you can type to and get answers from, like a text conversation.
People who write the script of a movie: what happens and what the characters say.
The people in charge of how a movie looks, such as the camera angles and lighting.
The money used in China. The article says 10m yuan is about 1.5m US dollars.
When a film opens in thousands of theaters at once instead of just a few.
Here, screens means individual movie-theater rooms. The film played in 10,000 of them.
Bombed means failed badly. A film that bombs earns much less money than hoped.
The money a film earns from ticket sales. It is how the movie business keeps score.
Here, grossed means earned in total, before costs are taken away. It has nothing to do with being disgusting.
So fast or confusing that it makes you feel dizzy. Constant jumps between shots made the film hard to watch.
In film, a cut is the moment one shot switches to another. Too many fast cuts feel chaotic.
In film, a shot is one piece of video filmed without a break. It is not the kind of shot from a vaccine or a basketball.
When things do not match or stay the same. The film's look kept changing from scene to scene.
To show or communicate. Good actors convey feelings through their faces.
Not like real life. The actors' faces moved in ways real faces do not.
Awkward and heavy, not smooth. A clunky film feels badly made.
Moving along slowly, so little seems to happen quickly.
A film made of drawn or computer-made pictures instead of filmed people, like a cartoon.
Spreading quickly across the internet as many people share it, like a germ spreading.
Shockingly or extremely. Here, so bad it was surprising.
Starting again at the very beginning, with nothing kept from earlier work.
To reach the same level as something that is ahead. The producers kept redoing the film so it matched newer AI tools.
People who work in a business and know it well from the inside.
Pictures made on a computer instead of filmed, often called CGI. It is used for special effects like dragons or explosions.
So interesting that you want to keep watching. Viewers pay for a compelling story.
Very short story videos, just minutes long, made for phones. They are hugely popular in China.
Very popular right now, like a fashion everyone follows.
Watched or listened to something. The phrase comes from tuning a radio or TV.
Here, productions are finished shows or films that were made.
A very popular short-video app in China. It is the Chinese version of TikTok.
To make lots of something quickly, often without much care, like butter being churned.
Silly and wacky in a funny way.
Here, fare means the kind of entertainment on offer. It is not the price of a bus ticket.
A famous ruling family of ancient China that governed about a thousand years ago.
Being planned or made but not finished yet.
A business that organizes and pays for making films or shows.
The film's title is named after a site in China known for ancient bronze treasures.
Told the public about something. A company announced its next film.
A lot. A film heavily using AI relies on it for much of the work.
Here, projects are jobs or works a company is making, like new films.
When people no longer remember something. The Economist jokes that the producers hope everyone forgets the flop.
